query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: is_not_recommended
per_column.rationale: This is a trivial binary inversion of the existing original 'Recommended' column. It carries no information not already present, so it adds no new analytical axis for a query that already keys on Recommended=no. Values are fully grounded (sample 1 glowing review -> 0, sample 2 negative review -> 1).

per_column.name: service_consistency_gap
per_column.rationale: A per-review consistency/gap metric could in principle help locate uneven service, but the produced values are opaque and, crucially, it is roughly the arithmetic negative of 'expectation_inflation' (sample1 -5.0 vs 5.0; sample4/5 -5.0 vs 5.0), making it a near-restatement. A review explicitly described as 'consistently good' still gets -5.0, so the value does not actually reflect 'consistency.' Likely computed from numeric rating columns present in the table, so not clearly invented, but weakly justified.

per_column.name: has_critical_service_failure
per_column.rationale: Flagging critical failures is topically relevant to improvement, but it fires on 73% of rows AND directly contradicts source text: 'Flight was amazing... 9/10' and 'Excellent performance on all fronts' are both marked =1. Assigning a critical failure to clearly glowing reviews is unsupported by the source, and the near-universal firing rate also blunts its discriminative value.

per_column.name: poor_value_perception
per_column.rationale: A thresholded 'poor value' flag gives a usable grouping axis for why passengers do not recommend, though it partly restates the existing 'Value For Money' rating. Sample values are consistent with the text (dreadful seats -> 1, amazing/excellent/good -> 0).

per_column.name: premium_with_low_rating
per_column.rationale: A genuine interaction axis (Class x low Overall Rating) that isolates high-value premium passengers who rated poorly -- directly actionable for the improvement query and not derivable from any single existing column alone. Samples are all 0 and consistent (all shown rows are either economy or high-rating).

per_column.name: high_service_variance
per_column.rationale: Overlaps conceptually with service_consistency_gap and adds limited independent leverage. Grounding is weak: 'Excellent performance on all fronts' (an explicitly uniform experience) is flagged as high variance =1, contradicting the source, though sample 1/4/5 are handled correctly.

per_column.name: expectation_inflation
per_column.rationale: An ambiguous gap-style score that broadly tracks review sentiment/Overall Rating (high for praise, negative for complaints) and is essentially the negative twin of service_consistency_gap, so it is largely redundant. Values are directionally consistent with the text and plausibly derived from rating columns, but they mostly re-encode existing rating signal.

judge.rationale: The set contains a couple of genuinely useful new axes (premium_with_low_rating isolates high-value dissatisfied customers; poor_value_perception offers a usable segmentation), but is diluted by redundancy and weak grounding elsewhere. is_not_recommended merely restates the original Recommended column; service_consistency_gap and expectation_inflation are near arithmetic mirrors of each other and largely re-encode the Overall Rating signal; high_service_variance overlaps the same consistency idea. Groundedness is mixed: several columns read the text soundly, but has_critical_service_failure and high_service_variance assign failure/variance flags to reviews explicitly described as 'amazing' or 'excellent on all fronts,' contradicting the source, and has_critical_service_failure fires on 73% of rows. Overall moderate quality on both necessary conditions.
